22646-the-hunters-of-the-ozark.title: Hunters Of The Ozark.
22646-the-hunters-of-the-ozark.creator: Edward S. Ellis
22646-the-hunters-of-the-ozark.description: A book by Edward S. Ellis. One day in the autumn Terence Clark came to the house of Frederick Linden and urged him to join in a hunt for a cow that had been missing since the night before. The latter got the consent of his mother and the two lads started on a search that proved to be the most eventful one they had ever known.

59402-betting-gambling-a-national-evil.title: Betting Gambling A National Evil
59402-betting-gambling-a-national-evil.creator: John A. Hobson
59402-betting-gambling-a-national-evil.description: A book by John A. Hobson. In tossing “heads or tails” for the possession of a coin, neither party has any knowledge or control of the adjustment of forces which determines upon which side the coin will fall, or if by practice the tosser acquires such knowledge or control, he cannot possibly predict or control the “call” of his opponent, which thus keeps the determination of the issue within the realm of “Chance.”

arxiv-2109-06002.title: Compact sets and the closure of their convex hulls in CAT(0) spaces Thanks: MSC: 52A05, 52A27, 54D30, 54E45, 30L05
arxiv-2109-06002.creator: Arian Bërdëllima
arxiv-2109-06002.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Arian Bërdëllima. We study the closure of the convex hull of a compact set in a complete CAT ⁡ ( 0 ) \CAT(0) space. First we give characterization results in terms of compact sets and the closure of their convex hulls for locally compact CAT ⁡ ( 0 ) \CAT(0) spaces that are either regular or satisfy the geodesic extension property. Later inspired by a geometric interpretation of Carathéodory’s Theorem we introduce the operation of threading for a given set.

arxiv-2201-02197.title: Isoperimetric 3- and 4-bubble results on ℝ \mathbb{R} with density | x | |x|
arxiv-2201-02197.creator: Evan Alexander, Emily Burns, John Ross, Jesse Stovall, Zariah Whyte
arxiv-2201-02197.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Evan Alexander, Emily Burns, John Ross, Jesse Stovall, Zariah Whyte. 1 Introduction The classic isoperimetric problem asks one to find, out of all simple closed curves in the plane with fixed perimeter P , the curve that encloses the maximal amount of area A . Equivalently, the iso-area problem asks one to find the simple-closed curve with minimal perimeter out of all simple closed curves with a fixed enclosed area.

arxiv-2206-13686.title: Thickness optimization of the output power and effective thermoelectric figure of merit of thin thermoelectric generator
arxiv-2206-13686.creator: Takao Ishida
arxiv-2206-13686.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Takao Ishida. The conventional thermoelectric figure of merit and the power factor are not sufficient as a measure of thin film quality of thermoelectric materials, where the power conversion efficiency depends on the film dimensions. By considering the film size, the effective thermoelectric figure of merit and effective Seebeck coefficient are introduced to guarantee that the maximum energy conversion efficiency increases as the effective thermoelectric figure of merit increases. Similarly, the effective power factor is defined.

arxiv-2207-14088.title: On the Sequential Probability Ratio Test in Hidden Markov Models
arxiv-2207-14088.creator: Oscar Darwin, Stefan Kiefer
arxiv-2207-14088.description: Abstract We consider the Sequential Probability Ratio Test applied to Hidden Markov Models. Given two Hidden Markov Models and a sequence of observations generated by one of them, the Sequential Probability Ratio Test attempts to decide which model produced the sequence. We show relationships between the execution time of such an algorithm and Lyapunov exponents of random matrix systems.

arxiv-2211-14364.title: Safe and Robust Observer-Controller Synthesis using Control Barrier Functions
arxiv-2211-14364.creator: Devansh R. Agrawal, Dimitra Panagou
arxiv-2211-14364.description: Abstract This paper addresses the synthesis of safety-critical controllers using estimate feedback. We propose an observer-controller interconnection to ensure that the nonlinear system remains safe despite bounded disturbances on the system dynamics and measurements that correspond to partial state information.

arxiv-2212-11885.description: Abstract . In an earlier paper, we described bordered algebras for knot Floer homology. In this paper, we introduce closely related differential graded algebra, the pong algebra , and compute the A ∞ A_{\infty} structure on its homology. 1. Introduction Knot Floer homology [ 13 , 21 ] is a knot invariant defined using methods from symplectic geometry.

arxiv-2406-05265.title: TLEX: An Efficient Method for Extracting Exact Timelines from TimeML Temporal Graphs
arxiv-2406-05265.creator: Mustafa Ocal, Ning Xie, Mark Finlayson
arxiv-2406-05265.description: Abstract A timeline provides a total ordering of events and times, and is useful for a number of natural language understanding tasks. However, qualitative temporal graphs that can be derived directly from text—such as TimeML annotations—usually explicitly reveal only partial orderings of events and times.

arxiv-2412-03163.title: Constraints on dark matter annihilation in the Large Magellanic Cloud from multiple low-frequency radio observations
arxiv-2412-03163.creator: Zhanfang Chen, Feng Huang, Taotao Fang
arxiv-2412-03163.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Zhanfang Chen, Feng Huang, Taotao Fang. Low-frequency radio emission from the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) is assumed to be dominated by nonthermal synchrotron radiation from energy loss of energetic e + / e − e^{+}/e^{-} in magnetic field. Two different kinds of sources of e + / e − e^{+}/e^{-} , dark matter (DM) annihilation and cosmic rays (CR) related to massive stars, are taken into account in this paper.

arxiv-2501-04512.title: Non-Markovianity increases transition path probability
arxiv-2501-04512.creator: Florian N. Brünig, Benjamin A. Dalton, Jan O. Daldrop, Roland R. Netz
arxiv-2501-04512.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Florian N. Brünig, Benjamin A. Dalton, Jan O. Daldrop, Roland R. Netz. Defining low-dimensional reaction coordinates is crucial for analyzing the dynamics of complex systems and for comparison with experiments. The maximal value of the transition-path probability along the reaction coordinate x x , p ⁡ ( TP | x ) p(\mathrm{TP}|x) , is a common estimator for reaction-coordinate quality by comparing to the theoretical maximal value of 1/2 in the overdamped Markovian limit.

arxiv-2503-21263.title: Cultivating Game Sense for Yourself: Making VLMs Gaming Experts
arxiv-2503-21263.creator: Wenxuan Lu, Jiangyang He, Zhanqiu Zhang †, Yiwen Guo †, Tianning Zang †, Institute of Information Engineering, Chinese Academy of Sciences, School of Cyber Security, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, School of Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Wuhan University of Technology, LIGHTS
arxiv-2503-21263.description: Abstract Developing agents capable of fluid gameplay in first/third-person games without API access remains a critical challenge in Artificial General Intelligence (AGI). Recent efforts leverage Vision Language Models (VLMs) as direct controllers, frequently pausing the game to analyze screens and plan action through language reasoning.

arxiv-2508-10480.description: Abstract We introduce an output layer for neural networks that ensures satisfaction of convex constraints. Our approach, Π \Pi net , leverages operator splitting for rapid and reliable projections in the forward pass, and the implicit function theorem for backpropagation.

pmc-11429668.title: Diabetic Kidney Disease: Contribution of Phenyl Sulfate Derived from Dietary Tyrosine upon Gut Microbiota Catabolism
pmc-11429668.creator: Haoxin Liu, Tram N Diep, Ying Wang, Yucheng Wang, Liang-Jun Yan, Theodoros Eleftheriadis
pmc-11429668.description: Deranged gut microbiota can release increased levels of uremic toxins leading to exacerbated kidney injury. In diabetic kidney disease (DKD), phenyl sulfate (PS) derived from tyrosine catabolism by gut microbiota has been demonstrated to be both an early diagnostic marker and a therapeutic target.

pmc-11525371.title: Revisiting the diagnostic performance of exosomes: harnessing the feasibility of combinatorial exosomal miRNA profiles for colorectal cancer diagnosis
pmc-11525371.creator: Jin Sung Park, Jin Ah Choi, Da Han Hyun, Chorok Byeon, Sang Gyu Kwak, Jun Seok Park, Seonki Hong
pmc-11525371.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The challenges associated with liquid biopsy of colorectal cancer (CRC) are closely linked to the substantial variations observed in gene expression profiles among patients. This variability complicates the selection of an ideal biomarker for accurate diagnosis. In this report, we propose that employing a combination of miRNAs offers a better change for enhancing the accuracy of CRC diagnosis compared to solely relying on single miRNAs.

pmc-12750851.title: Understanding patient preferences on providing sociodemographic information in an acute care setting: a qualitative study
pmc-12750851.creator: Yasmin Garad, Negin Pak, Bronwyn Barker, Danielle Kasperavicius, Joshua Pratt, Seema Marwaha, Michael Colacci, Reena Pattani, Elizabeth Kipp, Joan Conrad, Sharon E. Straus, Christine Fahim
pmc-12750851.description: BackgroundAccess to patient sociodemographic information is a critical factor to understanding, at a systems-level, where health inequities exist so they can be addressed. Patient concerns around disclosing personal information remain a barrier to sociodemographic data collection. Our objective was to assess patient perceptions regarding the routine collection of sociodemographic information in an acute care hospital setting.

pmc-13374290.title: Extracellular vesicles from chemotherapy-induced senescent tumor cells reprogram hepatic phospholipid metabolism to promote pancreatic cancer liver metastasis
pmc-13374290.creator: Bai’an Tao, Yecheng Xu, Wenteng Miao, Zhenmei Chen, Jichun Gu, Yujie Guo, Linjie Chen, Yang Di, Hang He, Chen Jin, Ji Li, Deliang Fu
pmc-13374290.description: BackgroundPancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a highly metastatic disease, with over one-third of patients developing liver metastasis following neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC). This study aimed to investigate how the effect of chemotherapy on the primary tumor shapes the hepatic pre-metastatic niches (PMNs), which remains poorly understood.MethodsRNA sequencing was performed in a PDAC cohort to identify transcriptomic features associated with metastasis.

pmc-13601064.title: Beyond weight loss: Disentangling the direct effects of semaglutide vs equivalent calorie restriction on reproductive systems of male and female rats
pmc-13601064.creator: Morgan R Sotzen, Suyeun Byun, Ngozi O Ibadin, Mya A Knappenberger, Madison T Bento, Mohammed Asker, Sergei Koshkin, Francisco J Diaz, Karolina P Skibicka
pmc-13601064.description: BackgroundSemaglutide (SEMA), a glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) analogue approved for treatment of obesity, is now one of the most used anti-obesity pharmacotherapeutic agents worldwide. The effects of SEMA on body weight, appetite, and adiposity are well established. Moreover, sex differences in these effects are clearly emerging.

pmc-13689518.title: When to wait and when to intervene: A retrospective study on predicting spontaneous clearance of common bile duct stones in ERCP candidates
pmc-13689518.creator: Mohammad Taghi Hamidian, Javad Shokry Shirvany, Maede Rajabi Fomashi, Ali Bijani, Seyed Hassan Abedi Valoukolaei
pmc-13689518.description: Background:While ERCP is a cornerstone in the management of choledocholithiasis, a significant proportion of common bile duct (CBD) stones may clear spontaneously, prompting the need for better risk stratification. To identify independent clinical, biochemical, and radiologic predictors of spontaneous CBD stone clearance in patients referred for ERCP.Methods:In this retrospective study, 324 patients with suspected choledocholithiasis were evaluated.

uslaw-usc-t18-s2.title: 18 U.S.C. § 2 — Principals
uslaw-usc-t18-s2.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t18-s2.description: United States Code, Title 18 (Crimes And Criminal Procedure); Part I (Crimes); Chapter 1 (General Provisions). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Whoever commits an offense against the United States or aids, abets, counsels, commands, induces or procures its commission, is punishable as a principal. (b) Whoever willfully causes an act to be done which if directly performed by him or another.
